title: Miracle health cure
post_text: BREAKING: Doctors confirm that drinking lemon water for three days can cure diabetes naturally. Pharmaceutical companies do not want you to know this.
red_flags: Unrealistic cure; no credible medical source; conspiracy framing; health risk
explanation: This should be reported because it makes a harmful medical claim without evidence. Medical claims need credible sources such as public health agencies, peer-reviewed research, or licensed professionals.
source_note: Scenario created for educational simulation; based on common misinformation patterns.

title: Scholarship payment scam
post_text: Congratulations! You were selected for a $10,000 international scholarship. Send a $75 processing fee today to unlock your award. Limited spots available.
red_flags: Requests money upfront; creates urgency; vague organization; too-good-to-be-true offer
explanation: This should be reported. Legitimate scholarships usually do not ask winners to pay a surprise fee through a direct message. The urgency and payment request are major warning signs.
source_note: Scenario created for educational simulation; based on common scholarship scam patterns.

title: AI-generated disaster image claim
post_text: This photo proves that a giant earthquake destroyed downtown last night. Share before the media deletes it!
red_flags: Emotional urgency; no date/location proof; asks users to share; dramatic claim without source
explanation: This deserves doubt. A dramatic image alone is not enough evidence. Users should verify the event through credible news, official emergency accounts, and reverse image search before sharing.
source_note: Scenario created for educational simulation; does not use a real disaster image.

title: Misleading statistic
post_text: 90% of students who use AI fail their exams. Schools are hiding the truth.
red_flags: No study cited; exaggerated statistic; vague group; fear-based wording
explanation: This is suspicious because it uses a precise statistic without naming a study, sample size, or source. Numbers can feel convincing even when they are unsupported.

title: Fake celebrity quote
post_text: Famous actor says: 'I never use vaccines because natural energy is enough.' This is why Hollywood is waking up.
red_flags: Quote has no original interview; appeals to celebrity authority; vague claim
explanation: This should be doubted. A quote needs a traceable source, such as an interview, verified account, or reputable publication. Celebrity authority does not replace evidence.

title: Real public safety alert
post_text: Local emergency services report heavy rain tonight. Avoid flooded streets and follow official updates from your city government account.
red_flags: Clear source type; practical advice; no sensational claim; verifiable guidance
explanation: This is likely trustworthy because it gives practical safety advice, avoids exaggerated claims, and points users toward official updates. Still, users should verify the account or source.

title: Phishing password reset
post_text: Your account will be deleted in 2 hours. Click this link immediately and enter your password to keep access.
red_flags: Threatening deadline; asks for password; suspicious link behavior; panic language
explanation: This should be reported as phishing. Legitimate services rarely ask users to enter passwords through urgent links in threatening messages.
source_note: Scenario created for educational simulation; based on common phishing patterns.

title: Manipulated screenshot rumor
post_text: Screenshot shows a school canceling all final exams. Someone sent it in a group chat, so it must be real.
red_flags: Screenshot can be edited; no official channel; relies on group chat rumor
explanation: This should be doubted. Screenshots are easy to edit or remove from context. Important school announcements should be verified through official channels.

title: Emotional manipulation post
post_text: Only heartless people will ignore this. Share this post if you care about children. If you do not share, you are part of the problem.
red_flags: Guilt pressure; false moral choice; no evidence; manipulative call to share
explanation: This deserves doubt because it pressures users emotionally instead of providing evidence. Manipulation often tries to make people share before thinking.

title: Transparent scientific update
post_text: A new study suggests that sleep quality may affect memory in teenagers. Researchers say more studies are needed before drawing final conclusions.
red_flags: Careful language; acknowledges uncertainty; avoids extreme claim
explanation: This is likely trustworthy because it uses cautious language and acknowledges uncertainty. Responsible scientific communication usually avoids absolute conclusions from one study.
